judgments.reasoning_cat1: A bare consideration/reliance preamble; nothing in it carries two reasonable meanings beyond ordinary OCR garbling.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It simply subjects everything to 'all the terms of this policy', which is consistent with the Declarations and the endorsement schedule.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The core insuring clause turns entirely on defined terms ('ultimate net loss', 'retained limit', 'occurrence', 'personal injury') and on the elastic phrase 'to which this policy applies', which litigants routinely read differently.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The trigger — an occurrence 'not covered by any underlying coverage ... or any other underlying insurance collectible by the insured' — leaves 'collectible' undefined and is a familiar site of argument.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A duty to defend 'even if such suit is groundless, false or fraudulent' coupled with a discretionary right to settle 'as it deems expedient' is standard but the two halves pull against each other.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A narrow, mechanical bond-premium obligation with an express disclaimer of any duty to furnish bonds; little to construe.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Standard costs-and-post-judgment-interest wording, capped by reference to the limit of liability; definite in operation.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Reimbursement of reasonable expenses other than loss of earnings, only when incurred at the company's request — a tightly bounded promise.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with c010, which makes supplementary payments additional to ultimate net loss.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Short and apparently definite, but 'covered by underlying insurance' is doing a lot of work where underlying cover is disputed or exhausted.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The condition 'immediately in excess of underlying insurance listed on the declarations page without intervening insurance' is a genuine operative qualifier that parties read differently.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The carve-out 'except settlement of claims or suits' is compressed and its reach over the preceding four sub-paragraphs is not obvious.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It bears on the Limit of Liability (c013/c084) by placing some sums outside the limit, but no direct contradiction appears.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Prevented by law or otherwise' is open-ended, and the substituted obligation (pay expenses incurred with written consent) is vaguely tied to 'this agreement'.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A clear reimbursement obligation keyed to Item 4 of the declarations; the wording itself is definite.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The aggregate proviso limits only products/completed-operations loss while the Declarations state a general aggregate, leaving the aggregate's reach uncertain on the face of the clause.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A stray fragment of a sub-paragraph; too little text to name a defect.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Conditional on the Named Insured being designated a partnership or joint venture, and the wording is the familiar form.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Standard two-limb property damage definition with a policy-period trigger; well settled wording.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Errors or omissions, malpractice or mistake of a professional nature' is a general formula whose reach over ordinary collection activity is uncertain.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A flat denial of medical malpractice coverage for any statutory health care provider, later contradicted within the same endorsement by the contingency grant — the opening sentence overstates its own effect.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A three-condition contingency with the further qualifier 'identified as being listed for contingency coverage purposes', a phrase whose referent is not supplied.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Item 7's schedule of underlying insurance identifies nothing as listed for contingency purposes, so the trigger points to something that does not exist in the instrument.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: It amends 'the Policy Territory provisions of the Hospital Professional Liability coverage part attached to the policy' and then merely recites a statute without stating an operative change.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Indemnity for 'legal or other expenses necessarily incurred ... in determining which insurer shall bear the loss' is an unusual and loosely bounded promise.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It sits against the ultimate net loss definition (c033), which excludes legal expenses from loss, and against the Other Insurance clause (c052), which itself allocates between insurers.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: It says coverage 'shall not apply to trebled damages' and then that the company will pay one-third of the total sum, and separately excludes plaintiff's legal fees twice by different routes — the mechanics are self-tangling.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Endorsement No. 5 (c111) deletes Form 009-133 and declares it null and void, yet the form remains in the assembled policy and on the endorsement schedule.
